I'll bid $221 to match the current high bid. I want p2 to win so the greens stay split, and I won't raise much beyond that.

P2's $220 bid is already above my preferred cap. P4 holds Penn and would need Pacific to complete a 2/3 green set. I should drop out since p2 is clearly ahead of p4.

I'm reconsidering dropping out. If I bid $221, p4 could still outbid p2 and claim the green set cheaply. Staying in with a small raise keeps pressure on p4 to pay more.

Pacific is a dead property without other greens, so it mainly blocks p4 from completing a 2/3 set. I can afford the $709 cash position after winning at $221. If I drop out, p4 will likely bid higher to claim the green set, while p2 may continue raising.

P2 may raise to $300. P4 might bid $250–$300 to complete a 2/3 green set. If I win at $221, the greens stay split exactly as if p2 held Pacific. The trade-off is spending $221 cash.

P4 holding Pacific would let them trade for North Carolina or buy it to form a green monopoly. That is the worst outcome. Bidding $221 risks stealing Pacific from p2 and winning an unwanted property. P2 may drop out if I raise, leaving me with a dead space. The better path is to stay out and let p2 win.

I'll bid $221 to keep p4 from sniping the auction. Dropping out would let them claim Pacific for at least $221, and I couldn't influence the price further.
